descriptions:
The essential Marrakech in one well-planned day, with a licensed local guide and a private driver, so you see the highlights without getting lost or rushed.

Your guide meets you at your hotel or riad and starts at the Koutoubia, the 12th-century mosque whose 77-metre minaret has been the city's landmark for almost 900 years; you walk through its rose gardens and learn how it inspired the Giralda in Seville. Next comes the Bahia Palace, built in the late 1800s for a grand vizier: room after room of carved cedar ceilings, painted doors, stucco and zellige tiles around courtyards of orange trees. Then the Saadian Tombs, the richly decorated mausoleum of a 16th-century dynasty, sealed off for centuries and rediscovered in 1917.

Around midday, the souks are at their liveliest. Your guide leads you through the lanes of leatherworkers, lantern makers, carpet dealers and spice sellers, explains how the markets are organised by trade and helps you bargain if you want to buy. After lunch, your driver takes you to the Majorelle Garden, the cobalt-blue villa and cactus garden restored by Yves Saint Laurent, before you end at Jemaa el-Fna as the food stalls set up, the smoke rises from the grills and the square fills with musicians and storytellers.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Koutoubia
09:45 – Bahia Palace
11:00 – Saadian Tombs
12:00 – Souks
13:30 – Lunch (not included)
15:00 – Majorelle Garden
17:30 – Jemaa el-Fna

WHY THIS ORDER
Monuments open early and are calmer before 11:00; the souks are liveliest around midday; Majorelle's timed tickets are easier in the afternoon; and Jemaa el-Fna is at its best as the food stalls set up at dusk.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Non-Muslims cannot enter the Koutoubia mosque; the gardens are open.
• The Saadian Tombs can have queues; your guide may swap them for El Badi Palace.
• Book Majorelle tickets online in advance.
• Wear comfortable shoes: most of the day is on foot in the medina.

INCLUDED: licensed guide, private driver for the longer distances, pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: entrance fees, lunch, tips.

WHAT YOU'LL TASTE
A tagine or tanjia (the slow-cooked Marrakech speciality) for lunch, fresh orange juice on the square, and mint tea to finish.

PHOTO SPOTS
• The Bahia Palace courtyards.
• The blue villa at Majorelle.
• Smoke rising from the food stalls at dusk.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: Marrakech's highlights, without stress.

faq.question: Can I see Marrakech in one day?
faq.answer: Yes, the main sights. This tour is designed for exactly that: the Koutoubia, the Bahia Palace, the Saadian Tombs, the souks, the Majorelle Garden and Jemaa el-Fna, in an order that avoids the queues and the midday heat. With a guide and a driver you don't lose time finding your way or arranging taxis.

faq.question: Are entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: No. Entrance fees for the Bahia Palace, the Saadian Tombs and the Majorelle Garden are paid on the spot or online. They are usually modest; Majorelle is the most expensive and sells timed tickets online, so book it a day ahead. Bring some cash in dirhams for the others.

faq.question: Is this a private tour?
faq.answer: Yes. Your guide and driver are for your group only, so you can ask questions, take your time where you like and skip what doesn't interest you. There is no minimum group size.

faq.question: What if I am only in Marrakech for a few hours?
faq.answer: Ask us for a half-day version focused on the medina: the Koutoubia, the Bahia Palace, the souks and Jemaa el-Fna, in about four hours. It's ideal on an arrival or departure day or as a cruise stop.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: No; your guide recommends a restaurant that fits your taste and budget, from a simple café serving tagines to a riad restaurant in a quiet courtyard. Vegetarian and gluten-free options are easy to find.

faq.question: How much walking is there?
faq.answer: Most of the day is on foot in the medina, around 6 to 8 km in total at an easy pace with many stops. The private car covers the longer distances, such as to the Majorelle Garden. Tell us if you'd like less walking, and we'll use the car more.

faq.question: What time does the tour start and end?
faq.answer: Usually from about 9:00 to 18:00, with pick-up and drop-off at your hotel or riad. As it's private, you can start later or end earlier; in summer, an early start is more comfortable.

faq.question: Is a licensed guide really necessary in Marrakech?
faq.answer: It makes a big difference on a first visit. A licensed guide knows the shortcuts through the medina, explains the history behind each monument and keeps unofficial guides and persistent sellers away, so you can enjoy the city calmly. Only licensed guides are allowed to guide visitors officially.

faq.question: Can children join the tour?
faq.answer: Yes. Children usually enjoy the snake charmers and musicians on the square, the colours of the souks and the garden at Majorelle. The guide adapts the pace, and the car makes it easy to take breaks. Bring water and sun hats in summer.

faq.question: What should I wear?
faq.answer: Light, comfortable clothes that cover shoulders and knees are respectful and practical in the medina. Wear closed, comfortable shoes, and bring sunglasses and a hat. A light scarf is useful against the sun.

faq.question: Will I be taken to shops?
faq.answer: Only if you want to go. Your guide can show you good places for leather, ceramics, lanterns or spices and help you bargain, but there is no obligation to buy and no compulsory shop stops. Tell your guide at the start what you're interested in.

faq.question: Is Marrakech safe to explore?
faq.answer: Yes, Marrakech is generally safe for visitors. The main nuisances are pickpockets in crowded places and persistent touts in the medina. With a licensed guide, you won't be bothered, and you can ask about anything, from tipping to taxis.

faq.question: When is the best time of year for this tour?
faq.answer: The tour runs all year. Spring and autumn are the most pleasant. In summer temperatures often pass 35–40 °C, so we start early and keep the shaded souks for the hottest hours. Winter days are sunny and mild, but evenings are cool.
